data.content_ref: inline:The target is internally inconsistent between its 'only if' constraint and its stated mechanism. The claim requires 'abandoning the claim that this methodology tracks truth or probability' and insists the preference is 'not a description of reality.' Yet the mechanism justifies the convention by asserting it 'maximizes the speed of error detection.' That is a substantive empirical conjecture about what the method achieves in the world — i.e., a description of reality. A pure conventionalist decision needs no outcome-based justification; by grounding the convention in a desirable consequence, the target smuggles back the very truth- or success-tracking commitment it declared illegitimate. Either the justification is purely conventional (in which case 'maximizes speed of error detection' is inadmissible loading), or the justification appeals to consequences (in which case the 'only if conventionalist / abandon truth-tracking' restriction is false). The target cannot coherently have both.
